edits.english: Ravina continued to inform Rav Pappa of Rava’s statements: Rava further raises another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered the animal for the sake of ordinary meat, it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type, i.e., for the sake of another offering, disqualifies the offering, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type, i.e., for the sake of ordinary meat, is disregarded and does not disqualify the offering.

And Rava raised another contradiction: Did Rav Yehuda say that Rav says that a sin offering that one slaughtered for the sake of a burnt offering is unfit, whereas if one slaughtered it for the sake of ordinary meat it is fit? Apparently, Rav holds that only improper intent that is of its type disqualifies it, whereas wrong intent that is not of its type does not disqualify it.

That something which is not of its type at all, such as ordinary (non-sacred) items regarding sacred items, is not considered something that can be applied to nullify the name of the offering from it (Rashi).
